👮 **Wachiman** · review of the whole pull request, at `b2705a9`: all 28 files reviewed.

5 finding(s): 1 to fix, 4 to consider; 5 on their lines. Reply in a comment's thread to answer it.

### Summary

**Batch 1 of 2.** Part 1 adds the floating \"Your video is ready\" window. It copies the capture toast's pattern: sender-checked card channels, validated payloads and actions, hand-offs that go through the main window's queued `sendToRenderer`, and a contract file with no value imports. Three findings, none of them blockers:\n\n- **Fix (medium confidence):** nothing closes the card when a new take or screenshot starts. Content protection is the only thing keeping it out of the result, and the repository's own `fullDisplayBorderAllowed` says that does not work on Windows builds before 19041, which paint a protected window black. On Linux, content protection does nothing, so the card would be recorded as it is. This is medium confidence because I did not confirm that the Windows and Linux builds are shipped.\n- **Consider:** the `recording-ready:show` handler accepts an invoke from any window, while the card's other channels check the sender.\n- **Consider:** going Back to the recording page floats the card again, because the asked-once ref is reset when the page remounts under the same history entry.

**Batch 2 of 2.** Part 2 covers the renderer wiring (render target, hand-offs, the recording page's ask with an in-app fallback), tests, CSS, docs and i18n. The routes for hand-offs reuse preparePath and editorPathFor. The fallback covers both a false answer and a rejected IPC, and the tests check that. The new `openFloatingHint` string is used by PostRecordingCard. There are two "consider" findings on the recording page. First, the ask waits for the probe, so a probe that never settles leaves no card at all, where the in-app card used to show right away. Second, the "asked" guard is a ref, so a router Back to the fresh recording's history entry floats the desktop card again.
